feature: A sheet of components whose states you can see and whose words you can read
summary: Ask and the skill now refuse a component whose states barely differ, whose surface vanishes into a white page, or whose words sit on words, run off a box or can't be read, in every state. A part can start hidden, so an Off checkbox is empty. Ask fixes those things itself instead of looping, and gets a title on every sheet.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no switch changed from its default. A new blank picture.

try.do: Make a new blank picture, press Command K and ask: create a table of apple like quality base components that show different states and text.
Look at the Checkbox row: Off is an empty box, On is checked.
Look at the Card and Alert rows: each sits on a visible card with a soft shadow, not words floating on white.
Compare it with the sheet from 2026-10-20.
Ask for a component sheet for a website's design system (buttons, fields, cards, nav).
Look at the same request made by the Photonz skill.
Open the sheet in the window and pick a look.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

evaluate: Can you tell every state from its neighbour at a glance?
Is every word on the sheet readable, in every state?
Do the empty cells (a toggle has no Hover column) bother you enough that rows should only show the states they have?
Is a hover a clear step darker or lighter the right amount of change, or too loud for an Apple-like kit?
rough: Not at the bar. Ask's judge lines are 5 to 6 of 10 (needed 8): component-table 59 and 51.1 on the final code (52 before this pass, 39.2 at the start), design-system-sheet 66.8 (52.8 before). Runs on the same code range from 37 to 59, so one run says little. The task stays open.

The skill is 83.6 on component-table (88.8 before; judge 7 to 8) and 82 on design-system-sheet (86.4 before; judge 6 to 8). Its judges now complain about the table, not the components: empty cells and a second header row.
Empty cells: rows whose kind lacks a state leave holes under the shared header, and every judge names them. Logged on this task, not filed.
What the model draws is still the limit for Ask: a dark Off track on a light page, a lumpy tab icon, buttons tight to a card's edge, a slider whose states look alike.
The window capture shows each copy's name chip over the header row; that is the-name-chips-over-component-copies-stay-clear.
